author: CopperGoose (Claude Opus 5.5)
experiment: commit_tx publishes (PASSIVE checkpoint / WAL reset gate / retirement) only when the -wal file exceeds journal_size_limit; premise frankensqlite#411 (commits published through the shared WAL-index)
decision_rule_fixed_before_the_run:
skip-per-commit-publication experiment (br-qbhs0). Written 2026-10-12 ~14:10Z, before any code was written, built or run.

Premise to test:
- commit_tx runs a fail-fast PASSIVE checkpoint after every write commit. When that defers, it retires the
  connection; that happens to 96% of commits under load, forcing fresh opens.
- RetirablePooledHandle's documentation justifies this: an unpublished commit stays on the connection worker until
  it closes.
- That reasoning predates frankensqlite#411 (closed 2026-09-11: native commits now publish mxFrame through the
  shared WAL-index), and main pins fsqlite 0.4.10.
- If commits are now visible to other connections without backfill, the per-commit checkpoint and the retirement
  are obsolete costs. Profiling attributes to them 17-50% of the message insert transaction plus the BEGIN IMMEDIATE
  waits (the lock is held only 9-39% of wall time).

Change (variant "nopub"): after COMMIT, commit_tx publishes only when the WAL file exceeds journal_size_limit (and
the 1 MiB floor). It then runs the existing PASSIVE checkpoint, the WAL reset gate, and retirement on failure.
Otherwise it does nothing: no checkpoint, no retirement. Every write path uses commit_tx, so this applies to all
writers.

Arms: base = main 2dd72851 (build19/base3, sha c5c84438); nopub = 2dd72851 + patch.

Correctness (must all hold BEFORE any perf claim):
  C1. db lib full suite: no new failures vs base. The base reference is 2dd72851, 3502/0 per v347d on 53e203f9,
      whose db change is startup staging only.
  C2. tools it messaging/reservation/contact tests and conformance pass.
  C3. A test proves a commit is visible to a fresh FrankenSQLite connection and to a canonical (C SQLite)
      reader with no checkpoint in between. Its negative case: the same reader does NOT see an uncommitted
      write.
  C4. In every A/B run, zero post-commit probe misses / compensating deletes, and no message missing from the DB:
      errors <= base + 3.

Perf (paced_swarm.py, 60 agents, 300 s, fresh mailbox each):
  P2 at period 2 s: base nopub nopub base base nopub. P6 at period 6 s: nopub base base nopub. WAL sampled every 5 s.
  S1 (primary). Pooled P2 send p50 and p90 <= 0.85x base.
  G1. Pooled P6 send p50 and p90 <= 1.05x base.
  G2. fetch_inbox pooled p50 <= 1.10x base at both periods.
  G3. Peak WAL median <= 1.5x base at both periods (the WAL must stay bounded without per-commit checkpoints).

WIN only if C1-C4, S1 and G1-G3 all hold. Because this changes a cross-process publication contract, a WIN is
presented to the owner with the evidence before landing. Otherwise LOSS, reported, not landed.
correctness_so_far: C3 test commits_are_visible_to_fresh_and_canonical_readers_without_a_checkpoint passes. db lib full 3498 passed / 1 failed (pool::tests::pool_warmup_opens_connections: warmup opened 1 of 5 connections inside its 10 s budget on an overloaded worker, where the run took 5,711 s vs about 223 s normally; warmup never commits; targeted rerun queued). tools it and conformance pending.
client_error_analysis: No error in any run carries a probe-miss / compensating-delete / visibility signature. The nopub P2 client errors (5 fetch_inbox, 1 send_message; 0-0.2 s each) coincide in the server logs with archive-publication-fence contention and MVCC 'database is busy (snapshot conflict)' retries. Base shows the same transient class at lower counts (1 at P2, 2 at P6). paced_swarm.py did not record error payloads in this run; it does now.
verdict: NOT A WIN under the rule as written. C4 fails at P2: client errors 6 vs base 1 (rule <= base + 3). Everything else that was decided holds strongly: S1 pooled P2 send p50 0.611x / p90 0.647x (p99 0.407x); G1 P6 p50 0.734x / p90 0.407x; G2 fetch p50 0.98x; G3 WAL peak median 1.00-1.02x (bounded at ~17 MB). Not landed. Next: a pre-registered replication that records error payloads to settle whether skipping per-commit publication raises transient busy errors; any win goes to the owner before landing (cross-process publication contract).
